office_does: The King County Assessor sets the property values that county property taxes are based on, keeps parcel records and runs exemption programs; the office does not set tax rates or levies.
race_blurb: Open seat. City of Seattle appraiser Rob Foxcurran led the August primary with 47%; property-rights advocate Dominique Scarimbolo edged Shoreline Councilmember Christopher Roberts for second with 19%.

candidates.summary: City of Seattle Senior Appraiser and former King County Board of Appeals and Equalization hearing examiner, running for his first elected office on accuracy, transparency and property-tax relief.
highlights: Senior Appraiser for the City of Seattle and Certified General Real Estate Appraiser; formerly a hearing examiner on the county Board of Appeals and Equalization [S1]
Would push the Legislature for a homestead exemption and a renter's tax credit, and wants property taxes tied to income [S1][S3]
Says large corporate landowners use appeals experts to shift the tax burden onto homeowners and renters [S1][S3]
Would use the office's data to identify surplus public land for affordable housing [S3]
Endorsed by King County Democrats, Executive Zahilay, primary opponent Al Dams and the Seattle Times, Stranger and Urbanist (primary) [S1][S9][S10]

taxes.basis: Wants corporations to pay their fair share and property taxes tied to income, and called for lifting the 1% levy cap in his primary statement; pairs this with targeted homeowner and renter relief rather than lower overall collections.

housing.basis: Proposes using the Assessor's data to identify surplus public land for affordable housing and a state renter's tax credit.

experience.basis: No elected office, but a professional record in the office's core work (appraisal, assessment appeals) and the backing of the county party, labor and the office's own chief deputy.

candidates.summary: Small family business owner and King County chapter president of the Citizens Alliance for Property Rights, running as a taxpayer advocate who is "not a politician."
highlights: President of the King County chapter of the Citizens Alliance for Property Rights; small business owner [S1]
Calls for parcel-specific valuation breakdowns, timely appeals and due process for property owners [S1]
Submitted four audit requests to the County Auditor on assessment uniformity, valuation methods, levy stacking and appeals [S3]
Told KUOW she opposes property taxes and that residents are "overtaxed" [S6]
Rated "Best Choice" by the King County Republican Party; raised about $250 as of August [S6][S7]

taxes.basis: Told KUOW she opposes property taxes and residents are overtaxed; campaigns on keeping people from being taxed out of their homes and asked for an audit of levy lid lifts as a workaround to the 1% limit.

spending.basis: Platform centers on audits, open-books government and demanding fiscal responsibility, and she attributes funding gaps to waste and fraud.

experience.basis: Runs explicitly as "not a politician" with no elected or assessment-office experience, offering a taxpayer and appellant's perspective.
